Text 1
Archaeologists have long viewed Stonehenge as a ceremonial site built by local farming communities. Its stones, they note, align with the sunrise at the summer solstice.

Text 2
Recent isotope analysis of animal bones from feasts near Stonehenge shows that many of the pigs eaten there were raised far away, some in what is now Scotland. Researchers conclude that people traveled great distances to gather at the site.
stem: Based on the texts, how does the finding in Text 2 most directly relate to the view in Text 1?
choices: It suggests that the site drew people from a far wider area than local communities alone.
It proves that Stonehenge was not used for the ceremonies connected to the summer solstice that Text 1 describes.
It shows that the stones of Stonehenge were brought from what is now Scotland.
It confirms that only local farmers raised the animals eaten at Stonehenge.
steps: Text 1: built and used by local farming communities, for ceremony.
Text 2: pigs from far away, so people traveled great distances to gather there.
That broadens who was involved without denying the ceremonial role.
It says nothing about solstice use or where the stones came from, and it contradicts “only local.”
key: Ask which part of Text 1 the new evidence extends or challenges.
